mechanism_boundary.composition: A corpus-only signed coordinate frontier generates candidates without the per-node graph walk; exact prefix/residual scoring refines encountered rows only as needed to establish the top100. The present task tests a necessary condition on the frontier component alone. It does not authorize a standalone TA/LEMP port.
mechanism_boundary.signed_access: Store one ascending list of(value,row-ID) pairs per original coordinate. Query sign chooses direction. Scores are original inner products, without normalization, learned coordinate selection or query-identity recognition.
mechanism_boundary.certificate: Unencountered rows are bounded by the sum of query-weighted current list-frontier values. Encountered rows must be fully scored or bounded rigorously; partial refinement cannot silently remove their bytes from the budget.
scope_exclusions: no synthetic100D transfer claim from lane B

fixed_necessary_test.data: All256 already exposed reserved learn queries, full256921-row original128D Llama base, existing true top100. No new holdout or official-query look.
unattainable_relaxations: true100th-IP threshold known before any work
every coordinate advanced4096 places even though total actual advances are capped4096
all encountered candidate scoring and deduplication free
fixed_necessary_test.rank_definition: After p sorted accesses the next unseen list entry has zero-based rank p. Use zero-based4096 (one-based4097), not4095. For q_j>=0 use the N-4097 element of ascending coordinate order; for q_j<0 use ascending zero-based4096; q_j=0 contributes zero.
fixed_necessary_test.proof: Each feasible allocation has0<=p_j<=4096 and sum p_j<=4096. Signed contribution lists are descending, so g_j(p_j)>=g_j(4096). Therefore its unexplored threshold T(p)=sum g_j(p_j)>=L=sum g_j(4096). If L exceeds the actual100th score, no allocation in this fixed-budget threshold-certificate family can stop. Because4096<N, reading every row cannot bypass the certificate. This proof does not rule out other certificates, layouts or approximate methods.
fixed_necessary_test.smallest_counter: E44 now uses the still cheaper Cauchy relaxation described below: extract two fixed coordinate order statistics and a certified corpus maximum squared norm, then evaluate256 exact signed frontier expressions. No gold threshold, sorted index, ANN search, parameter sweep or query/base dot scan. The original pinned-GT test remains separate if Cauchy is inconclusive.
fixed_necessary_test.numerics: Validate finite f32 inputs, exact shape/byte lengths and all hashes. Use exact dyadic sums or outward arithmetic intervals for q-weighted frontier values. Recompute the gold boundary dot products from pinned original f32 rows/queries and verify agreement with scores.f64 and truth.u32, accounting for the original float64 reduction error. A certified lower endpoint greater than the threshold upper endpoint is a rejection witness. Equality/overlap is inconclusive, not a pass. Tie handling is descending score then ascending row ID.
fixed_necessary_test.rejection: Any certified L>threshold rejects this exact4096-budget family. Still retain all256 query intervals, margins, source IDs and aggregate counts. No wider cursor budget, alternate coordinate rotation, subset selection or weakened precision/recall rescue.
fixed_necessary_test.non_rejection: Cauchy non-rejection is explicitly inconclusive and leaves the original pinned-GT bound pending. A later non-rejection by that stronger bound only permits a separately registered actual candidate/work counter. Neither proves a feasible schedule.
fixed_necessary_test.retained_work: Report sorted accesses, frontier updates, unique candidate IDs, full/partial coordinates, exact multiply/add counts, heap operations, metadata/visited/cache reads+writes/resets, and total logical bytes independently. No floating-product/int8-product equivalence or bytes-to-QPS conversion.

E44_numerical_proof.supported_inputs: Little-endian finite IEEE binary32 bit patterns only, dimension exactly128; production fixture N256921,Q256. Negative zero and subnormals are supported. NaN/infinity, wrong hash/size/dimension, unsupported binary64 format or integrity mismatch fail the experiment.
E44_numerical_proof.ordered_statistics: Transform finite raw u32 bits b to (~b)&0xffffffff when negative, or b^0x80000000 otherwise. Unsigned integer order is exact numeric f32 order, with -0 before +0, whose values are equal. Partition uint32 keys at zero-based4096 and N-4097; invert selected keys exactly. Thus host float32 flush/rounding behavior cannot alter order statistics.
E44_numerical_proof.exact_query_arithmetic: Decode sign/exponent/significand from raw bits to Fraction. L=sum q_j*frontier_j and Q=sum q_j² are exact rational values. Query sign selects the frontier; zero contributes zero. L²-Q*M is compared exactly, and L>0 is mandatory before squaring can prove anything.
E44_numerical_proof.exact_promotion: For e=0, abs(x)=mantissa*2^-149; otherwise abs(x)=(2^23+mantissa)*2^(e-150). Convert the at-most24-bit nonnegative integer significand to binary64 exactly and apply an exact power-of-two scale. All nonzero promoted values are normal binary64, including source f32 subnormals. No hardware f32 arithmetic/conversion is required.
E44_numerical_proof.products: Each finite binary32 square has at most48 significant bits, so binary64 multiplication is exact. Nonzero squares lie between2^-298 and less than2^256, safely inside normal binary64;128-term sums are below2^263. Therefore no underflow/overflow rounding term is omitted.
E44_numerical_proof.sum_error: Compute every row norm using a separate binary64 square array and127 explicit np.add steps, starting with the first square. With u=2^-52, each correctly rounded normal binary64 addition has relative error magnitude<=u even under a directed IEEE rounding mode; this deliberately uses a looser u than round-to-nearest2^-53. gamma127=127*u/(1-127*u). Positive-sum analysis gives |s_hat-s|<=gamma127*s, hence s<=s_hat/(1-gamma127).
E44_numerical_proof.maximum_and_outward_step: Selecting max(s_hat) is comparison only, with no arithmetic rounding. Convert that binary64 value to its exact Fraction and divide by exact(1-gamma127). This rational M bounds every true corpus row norm²; no rounded gamma, denominator, division, square root or final comparison enters the certificate. The encoded upper bound itself need not be binary64.
E44_numerical_proof.Cauchy_relaxation: For every row x, q dot x <= ||q||*||x|| <= sqrt(Q*M). Therefore true100thIP <= sqrt(Q*M). If exact L>0 and exact L²>Q*M, then L>true100thIP. Replacing the true threshold with this larger ceiling can only remove rejection witnesses, never create a false witness.
E44_numerical_proof.interpretation: Certified rejection concerns only the fixed4096-access threshold-certificate family. Nonpositive L, equality or nonpositive squared margin is inconclusive; it is never a feasibility, performance or recall pass.
E44_numerical_proof.retention: Retain all256 query ordinals, exact L/Q/squared margin, positivity/rejection flags, selected frontier bit patterns, gamma and M fractions, maximum computed norm's hex value and row witness, source hashes and numerical environment.
E44_numerical_proof.runtime: E44 main cap<=180s. All source arrays are hashed and byte/shape-checked; only base.f32 and validation.f32 are read. No labels, candidate search, official queries, full sorted index, full-query dot-product scan, build, install or paid call.
E44_numerical_proof.checker: frontier_bound_check.py independently checks raw-f32 decoding/order/signs, fixed-rank off-by-one boundaries, exact Cauchy sign/equality boundaries and numerical norm enclosures against Fraction sums, including extreme finite/subnormal inputs. The main run requires a successful receipt matching both source hashes.
